PJ04.title: Change order: raise -> approve / reject / cancel (G5 - never walked)
PJ04.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28 as a real WORKER (SET LOCAL ROLE authenticated + request.jwt.claims), every probe inside a transaction that ROLLED BACK. THE WALK REFUTED MY OWN GROUND FINDING, which is the most useful thing it did. G4 claimed 'one permissive ALL policy per table means any active member can approve a change order'. I had asserted that from the POLICY layer alone and it is WRONG: wh_guard_supervisor_approval() is a TRIGGER over six tables and project_change_orders is one of them - I had even written that list into the AHK1 gate label earlier in the same session and still did not check it here. Measured: approve -> BLOCKED, reject -> BLOCKED (the AH3 clause working), edit an APPROVED CO's cost -> BLOCKED ('remove signed-off work'). Recall the disposition before declaring a bug. WHAT IS ACTUALLY OPEN, and it is sharper than what I guessed: the guard protects the approval ACT and signed-off work, and nothing protects the CONTENT or the EXISTENCE of a request awaiting review. Proven live - worker Bryan Garcia rewrote worker Wilfredo Malabanan's PENDING change order from PHP 500,000 to PHP 9,999,999 and replaced its scope text, and the row still reads requested_by = Wilfredo Malabanan. A worker can also DELETE a pending CO outright. Combined with G1 (no auth_uid on the table) and G2 (no audit trigger on projects), nothing records that it changed or who changed it: the supervisor approves what they are SHOWN, and what they are shown is editable by anyone in the hive. A FIXTURE WEAKNESS FOUND EN ROUTE: my seeder assigns every CO in a hive the same requested_by (m.rn=2), so the first 'can a worker edit ANOTHER's CO' probe returned UPDATE 0 and looked like a block. It was not - there was simply no other requester's row to match. Inserting one made the tamper succeed immediately. UPDATE 0 is not evidence of a guard; it is the 0-row-write-is-not-an-error lesson in probe form. FIX/GATE still open. FIXED by 20260728000022: a raised change order's COMMERCIAL TERMS are immutable (cost, schedule, scope, title, requester, project, hive) and it cannot be DELETED - cancel instead, so the request stays visible in the amendment trail. Status and the approver fields stay mutable, with wh_guard_supervisor_approval still deciding who may move them. LEGITIMATE CALLERS MEASURED FIRST, because twice in the previous arc the obvious guard would have broken more than the bug: there are exactly THREE update paths on this table in the whole codebase (approveCO/rejectCO/cancelCO), all of which set status plus approver fields and nothing else; there is NO edit-CO path anywhere and NO delete path in any page or edge fn. The terms were already write-once in practice, so making the DATABASE agree breaks zero callers - and immutability is a stronger guarantee than a role check. VERIFIED: worker cost-tamper -> blocked, delete -> blocked, worker cancel -> still allowed, SUPERVISOR APPROVE -> still allowed (UPDATE 1).

PJ07.title: Earned Value - is green/amber/red defensible? (EVM / PMBOK)
PJ07.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. MY OWN GROUND NOTE WAS WRONG AND IS CORRECTED HERE. I judged the client fallback's 'hoursActual * 200' and invented-looking 0.95/0.85 bands WITHOUT reading the implementation it falls back FROM. python-api/projects/diagnostic.py is well-founded: it cites PMI PMBOK 7th ed. (Measurement) and AACE International RP 80R-13, states every formula in its docstring (PV/EV/AC/SV/CV/SPI/CPI), attributes the green/amber/red bands to AACE EV interpretation guidance rather than inventing them, and REFUSES when inputs are missing - {available:false, reason:'Requires budget_php + start_date + end_date'} - which is precisely the refusal path PJK2 asks for. DEFAULT_LABOR_RATE_PHP_PER_HOUR = 200 is a documented DEFAULT PROXY with a stated upgrade path ('Phase 5 will pull from worker_profiles') and is overridable per call. Recall the disposition before declaring a bug - twice in this arc now. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG, and it is narrower and sharper: (1) THE OVERRIDE IS DEAD. project-manager.html never passes labor_rate_php_per_hour - 0 matches in the file - so the parameter exists, is documented, and is never supplied. Every project on the platform is costed at PHP 200/hour regardless of trade or region, and CPI is EV/AC, so CPI is off by exactly the ratio of the real rate to 200. (2) TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE METRIC. clientRollup() re-implements EVM in the browser with the same constants and the same bands but NO citation, so the standard-citing version and the unattributed copy can drift apart with nothing detecting it. (3) THEY ALREADY DISAGREE. Both weight pct_complete by estimated_hours, but the client wraps it in Math.round() and the server keeps the float. EV = BAC x (pct/100), so rounding pct to an integer moves EV by up to 0.5% of BAC - on the seeded PHP 1,850,000 project that is about PHP 9,250 of Earned Value, and it is the CLIENT number a supervisor sees when the edge fn has not answered. FIX/GATE open: the shape is a single source of truth for the bands + rate (register the formula in canonical/formula_contracts.json as AH7's Action Priority was), the page passing a real rate, and a gate asserting the client fallback cannot diverge from the cited implementation.

PJ08.title: Critical path - what decides that a task may slip?
PJ08.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THE SERVER IMPLEMENTATION IS SOUND, and saying so is half the value of the walk: python-api/projects/prescriptive.py cites PMBOK 7th ed. §6.5.2.2 (Critical Path Method) and AACE 24R-03 (Forensic Schedule Analysis), uses networkx.dag_longest_path() rather than hand-rolled graph code, documents the forward/backward pass (ES/EF/LF/LS, slack = LS - ES, critical = slack 0), and carries real refusal paths - no items returns an empty critical path, and a missing networkx returns a stated cycle_warning instead of guessing. Its own docstring records that the PREVIOUS hand-rolled TS version silently miscomputed cycles and that networkx.find_cycle() now raises cleanly. That is the AHK2/PJK2 bar being met. A GOOD CONTRAST WITH PJ7, and it sharpens that finding: the client NEVER recomputes the critical path - 0 matches for any client-side CPM - it only reads _progress.critical_path. So the same page handles its two computed numbers with two different disciplines: the schedule verdict has ONE implementation, while Earned Value has a second, uncited copy in the browser that already diverges on rounding. THE DEFECT FOUND: an absence rendered as a VERDICT. renderCpm defaulted to {item_ids: [], total_days: 0, slack_per_item: {}} whenever the rollup was unavailable, so every task drew as NON-critical with ZERO slack. That is a positive answer where there should be none, and a self-contradictory one - zero slack is normally exactly what MAKES a task critical. Same shape as the is_anomaly defect in the Asset Hub arc. FIXED: the pane now says the critical path could not be computed and that nothing is therefore marked critical or slack-free, rather than quietly asserting a clean schedule.

PJ09.title: Budget: can a non-supervisor read it anyway? (G6)
PJ09.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. G6 CONFIRMED LIVE, and it is a UI-only gate on commercially sensitive data. renderBudget() tells a non-supervisor 'Budget visibility is restricted to supervisors' while projects_hive_rw grants every active member SELECT. Probed as worker Bryan Garcia: read budget_php straight off the table - CAP-2026-001 PHP 1,850,000 and CON-2026-001 PHP 280,000. The page renders a refusal; the database hands it over. WIDER THAN THE PANE: budget_php is in the MAIN project-list select (line 989) for every user, not just supervisors, and BAC is then computed client-side - so the number is already in the browser of everyone who opens the page, before any pane decides whether to show it. It is also exposed through v_project_truth. LEGITIMATE READERS MEASURED: the page itself (list select + the edit form + the client-side EVM), and two edge fns (project-orchestrator, project-progress) which run service-role and are unaffected by a client-side tightening. FIX/GATE open - the shape that fits this codebase is the one used twice already this session: move the privileged read into a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that checks supervisor role itself, drop budget_php from the client select, and let the edge fns keep their reach. PARTIAL FIX 2026-07-28 (mig ...023), and the partiality is stated deliberately rather than rounded up: get_project_budget() is a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that returns budget_php + the EVM dates ONLY to an active supervisor of that hive, using the same predicate as wh_guard_supervisor_approval so authority lives in one place. Verified both ways - supervisor gets PHP 1,850,000; worker gets {ok:false, reason:'not a supervisor'} with a stated detail rather than a silent null, so a refusal is not mistaken for 'this project has no budget'. THE HOLE IS NOT YET CLOSED and it would be dishonest to mark this journey done: the RPC adds a SANCTIONED path, it does not remove the unsanctioned one. A worker can still db.from('projects').select('budget_php') because RLS is row-level. Closing it needs three things together, which is why it is the next slice rather than a quick follow-on: REVOKE SELECT (budget_php) ON projects FROM authenticated (Postgres column privileges - the only mechanism that can withhold ONE column of a readable row), drop budget_php from the page's list select at line 989 and route renderBudget/clientRollup through the RPC, and decide what v_project_truth should expose, since it carries the column too. The edge fns are unaffected either way - both run service-role. BLAST RADIUS WIDENED 2026-07-28, and it turned the closure into a PRODUCT FORK rather than an engineering task. project-report.html renders 'Budget: PHP X' and computes BAC with NO supervisor gate of any kind (no isSupervisor, no HIVE_ROLE check anywhere in the file) - it only requires sign-in. It also feeds the budget into the AI companion context. And it reads v_project_truth with select('*'), as does project-orchestrator. SO A REVOKE WOULD BREAK IT: v_project_truth is security_invoker, so revoking SELECT(budget_php) on the base table propagates to the view, and a select('*') against a column the caller cannot read fails outright. project-orchestrator is service_role and unaffected; project-report is a CLIENT page and would break for supervisors too. THE REAL QUESTION IS NOT TECHNICAL. project-manager says budget is supervisor-only; project-report is a printable, signed-off client document whose own meta description is 'cost vs budget' and whose footer reads 'By signing below, the parties acknowledge...'. Those are two contradictory intents about who may see the figure, and which one is correct decides whether I gate the report or instead remove project-manager's false claim. That is Ian's call, not mine - putting a supervisor gate on a client sign-off document would change what the document IS. CLOSED 2026-07-28 (mig ...024) after Ian chose supervisor-only EVERYWHERE. THE COLUMN-LEVEL REVOKE ALONE WAS A NO-OP, and only a live check caught it: Postgres tests TABLE-level privilege first, so while GRANT SELECT ON projects TO authenticated stood, REVOKE SELECT (budget_php) changed nothing - column_privileges still listed authenticated on the column and a worker still read the figure. The working mechanism is to DROP the table-wide grant and re-GRANT the allowed columns explicitly, with the list GENERATED from information_schema rather than typed, since one missed column is an instant 42501 on a page that used to work. v_project_truth also had to lose the column: it is security_invoker, so a revoked base column would have made every select('*') against the view fail - and project-report.html and project-orchestrator both do exactly that. MY FIRST DRAFT OF THAT VIEW WAS WRITTEN FROM MEMORY AND WAS BADLY WRONG - it omitted all EIGHT correlated subqueries the pages depend on (item_count, items_done, estimated/actual_total_hours, last_progress_at, approved_change_orders, approved_co_cost_php, link_count), renamed actual_end_at, replaced the project_links-based maintenance_nature with a naive type map, and dropped the status<>'archived' filter. Dumping pg_get_viewdef first is the only reason the applied version is correct - the third time this session that rule has paid for itself. PAGE SIDE: budget_php removed from the shared list select; openDetail's select('*') enumerated explicitly (it would have 42501'd for everyone); the edit form prefills from the RPC and the save path OMITS the key entirely when the caller could not read it, because sending null would ERASE the budget - a blank field means withheld, never zero; clientRollup asks the RPC and simply renders no EVM block without a figure. VERIFIED at the privilege boundary, which is where the claim lives: worker direct read -> permission denied; worker other columns -> fine; worker select('*') on the view -> fine (22 cols, no budget, rollups intact, security_invoker preserved); worker RPC -> refused WITH a reason; supervisor RPC -> PHP 1,850,000. AN INSTRUMENT ERROR EN ROUTE, the third today: my first RPC test failed with 'permission denied' and looked like the fix breaking its own RPC - but the ARGUMENT subquery said WHERE budget_php IS NOT NULL, which runs as the CALLER. The RPC was never at fault. FOLLOW-UP LOGGED, not silently widened: v_project_truth still exposes approved_co_cost_php, also a financial figure readable by any member. Ian's decision covered the BUDGET; expanding it unasked would be scope creep on a security change.

PJ10.title: Roles: assign, remove, and what a role actually gates (G5)
PJ10.notes: GROUND 2026-07-28. The G5 fixture is BUILT, which is the prerequisite this journey could not start without: project_change_orders held ZERO rows platform-wide, so approve/reject/cancel had never run against data. Seeded all four states with their companion fields generated TOGETHER so no row is fiction - approved carries an approver AND a timestamp and no reason; rejected carries a REASON and no approved_at; pending and cancelled carry neither. Verified 0 incoherent rows across 12 COs (3 per state). project_roles likewise went 0 -> 36. A DEFECT CAUGHT IN MY OWN SEEDER BEFORE IT SHIPPED: the first draft wrote role='lead'/'member', but the CHECK allows only owner|planner|safety_officer|cost_engineer|reviewer. The insert would have been rejected while the seeder's try/except logged a WARN and returned an empty list - leaving the table exactly as empty as it started and looking seeded. Same shape as the Asset Hub is_anomaly defect: a value the CHECK forbids, failing quietly. Verified against pg_constraint, not guessed. WALK still to do.

PJ12.title: Delete a project - what goes with it, and is it recorded? (G2)
PJ12.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28. THREE MEASURED FACTS. (1) A WORKER COULD SOFT-DELETE ANY PROJECT IN THEIR HIVE. deleteProject() sets deleted_at, the button carries no role check, and neither did the database - projects_hive_rw is a single PERMISSIVE FOR ALL testing only membership. Probed live: an ordinary worker hid SHD-2026-001, a shutdown project they do not own, and every view filters deleted_at IS NULL so it vanishes for everyone. (2) NOTHING RECORDED IT - the G2 ground finding confirmed live: hive_audit_log held ZERO rows for target_type='projects' or any project-named action. A project could disappear and the log could not say it had ever existed, let alone who removed it. (3) A HARD delete cascades to ALL SIX child tables (every FK is ON DELETE CASCADE), and it is currently refused for any project carrying a change order because 20260728000022's immutability trigger fires on the cascade. That is an ACCIDENTAL side effect of a fix aimed at something else. Recorded rather than left to be discovered: nothing legitimate breaks today because the UI only soft-deletes, but a future admin hard-delete WILL fail with a change-order error that reads as unrelated. FIXED (mig ...026): removing or restoring a project is a supervisor act and is recorded either way, with the children counted BEFORE the statement because after a cascade there is nothing left to describe what was lost - the same reason trg_asset_node_delete_audit is a BEFORE trigger. Guarded rather than forbidden, because soft-delete is the intended workflow. VERIFIED: worker soft-delete -> blocked with a plain reason; worker ORDINARY EDIT -> still works (no over-blocking, which is the failure mode a broad guard invites); supervisor delete -> succeeds AND writes the platform's first ever projects audit row: 'Leandro Marquez | delete_project | SHD-2026-001 | 1 COs, 7 items'. The three new actions are registered in hive.html's ACTION_ICON with EN+FIL labels and their valence, so the trail is READABLE rather than a row of unlabelled dots - the exact gap the audit-coverage gate caught earlier today.

PJ13.title: Cross-hive: a foreign project's items / COs cannot leak or be written (G3)
PJ13.notes: WALKED 2026-07-28, and this is the probe that EARNS PJK4 rather than assuming it from the AHK4 analogy. READS ARE CORRECTLY ISOLATED, measured first and worth recording as a real result: as a member of one hive, projects / project_items / project_change_orders all return 0 rows for another hive. WRITES HAD THE PM13 GAP - with MY hive_id and ANOTHER hive's project_id, all three were ACCEPTED: a project_item, a progress log, and a CHANGE ORDER attached to a project the writer cannot even see. An APPROVED change order was refused, but by wh_guard_supervisor_approval on the STATUS, not by anything tenancy-related - worth stating so the next reader does not mistake that for isolation. INSTRUMENT NOTE, and it nearly produced a false clean: my first two probes failed with 23514 (a status enum I got wrong) and 23502 (a NOT NULL I omitted). Neither is 42501. Verify WHAT blocked a write, never merely THAT something did - the same trap AH13 hit on the reliability tables. SEVERITY MEASURED, AND HONESTLY CONTAINED - TODAY. v_project_truth's rollup subqueries (item_count, estimated_total_hours, approved_change_orders, approved_co_cost_php, link_count) carry NO hive filter; they are plain WHERE pi.project_id = p.id. What keeps an injected row out of the VICTIM's numbers is that the view is security_invoker, so those subqueries execute as the READER and RLS hides the foreign row. Proven: injecting an item with 999 estimated hours left the victim's rollup at 7 items / 33.00 est hrs, and the victim could not see the row. FIXED ANYWAY (mig ...025, five RESTRICTIVE parent-hive policies) because that containment rests ENTIRELY on security_invoker staying ON - and earlier the SAME DAY a routine CREATE OR REPLACE silently cleared that exact option from v_sensor_truth, since CREATE VIEW does not carry reloptions forward. One such slip on v_project_truth turns every unfiltered rollup subquery into a cross-tenant read, instantly and silently. Closing it at the WRITE removes the dependence on that option and on every future consumer remembering to be hive-scoped. 0 existing rows violated the new policies, so nothing that exists was rejected. VERIFIED: foreign -parent item and change-order inserts both blocked BY NAME (the policy is named in the error, which is far more diagnosable than the 23514 confusion above), and a legitimate own-hive write still succeeds. GATE validate_project_tenancy, teeth proven by dropping a policy -> FAIL on exactly that table.

PJK1.name: A money decision needs an identity and a trail
PJK1.notes: OPEN on measured ground (2026-07-28). Six of seven project tables have NO auth_uid column at all - only `projects` has one - so raising or approving a CHANGE ORDER, which is a contract amendment, is attributable to nobody. And `projects` appears nowhere in hive_audit_log.target_type while assets, logbook, inventory_items, marketplace_listings, marketplace_sellers, worker_profiles and amc_briefings all do. AHK1 covered an approval DECISION on a forgeable name; here the identity column does not exist and the trail is absent entirely. DETECT COMPLETE 2026-07-28: measured via pg_attribute that auth_uid exists on `projects` ONLY - project_items, project_change_orders, project_progress_logs, project_roles, project_links and project_knowledge have no such column - and via a DISTINCT on hive_audit_log.target_type that `projects` has never written one audit row. The change-order schema makes it concrete: requested_by text NOT NULL and approved_by text, on a row carrying cost_impact_php and schedule_impact_days. project_roles.assigned_by is a text name too. SWEEP/FIX/GATE open. GATE 2026-07-28: validate_change_order_immutability. It asserts the trigger still covers UPDATE AND DELETE (losing DELETE silently restores the make-it-disappear path), that every commercial term is still named in the immutability check (a term quietly dropped from that list becomes editable again - exactly the failure this arc found), that status/approved_by/approved_at/rejection_reason are NOT frozen because freezing them would break the lifecycle the table exists for, and LIVE that the trigger is attached and ENABLED - a disabled trigger looks present and enforces nothing. Teeth proven by unfreezing cost_impact_php: FAIL on exactly that term. STILL OPEN for this class, and stated rather than rounded up: the ATTRIBUTION half. Six of seven project tables still have no auth_uid, and `projects` still writes nothing to hive_audit_log, so a change order is now tamper-EVIDENT-by-construction but still not ATTRIBUTABLE.

PJK2.name: A schedule/health number must be falsifiable
PJK2.notes: OPEN. renderCpm reads _progress.critical_path (item_ids, total_days, slack_per_item) and renderBudget reads _progress.earned_value (bac, pv, and a green/amber/red status), both computed in the project-progress edge fn with no in-repo oracle found at ground. AHK2 governed inspection TIMING; these decide which work may slip and what health a CLIENT is told. EVM has published formulas (CPI=EV/AC, SPI=EV/PV) so the thresholds are checkable against a standard, exactly as AH7's RPN was.

PJK3.name: Authority must be enforced where the data is
PJK3.notes: OPEN. Every project table carries ONE permissive FOR ALL policy whose WITH CHECK tests only hive_id IN user_hive_ids() - so any active member can approve, reject or cancel a change order. project_roles is the only table with a supervisor predicate. Separately, renderBudget refuses non-supervisors in the RENDERER ('Budget visibility is restricted to supervisors') while projects_hive_rw grants every member read - the number is one db.from('projects') away. Sharpens feedback_ui_only_approval_gate_is_bypassable from a button to a whole pane. DETECT COMPLETE 2026-07-28: all seven policies dumped from pg_policy - each is a single PERMISSIVE FOR ALL whose WITH CHECK tests only auth.uid() IS NOT NULL AND hive_id IN user_hive_ids(). project_roles_supervisor_all is the ONLY one with a supervisor predicate. So the approve/reject/cancel buttons are gated by nothing but hive membership. Separately renderBudget refuses non-supervisors in the RENDERER while projects_hive_rw grants every member SELECT. SWEEP/FIX/GATE open - the live probe (read the budget as a worker) is the next unit.
